[ASSISTANT_SAID] Expanding the farm's product line to include homemade jam and honey can diversify offerings and attract new customers.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] For jam regulations, check if the state has cottage food laws allowing the sale of low-risk foods from home kitchens, which may require registration, labeling, and adherence to guidelines.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Food safety certification may be required in some states for cottage food operations, but it is often recommended even if not mandatory.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Registration for selling jams and honey typically involves registering with the state's department of agriculture, which may require a fee and could be a one-time or annual renewal.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] For jams, an ingredient list and allergen warning are required, but a nutrition facts label is not mandatory.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] For honey, only the net quantity and product name need to be included on the label.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] General labeling guidelines include truth-in-labeling, clear and conspicuous information, and proper font size and placement.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Repurposing an old plow can be a unique, cost-effective, and environmentally friendly gardening option, but it may require maintenance and safety checks.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Ideas for repurposing the old plow include using it as a garden bed edger, trellis, soil aerator, or decorative planter.
